newsitem.title: GERMANY: F.O. LICHT - Daily sugar report.
newsitem.headline: F.O. LICHT - Daily sugar report.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.
White sugar futures in London ended little changed in quiet dealings. March ended just 10 cents firmer at $297.70, while May last traded down 10 cents at $298.00, maintaining the nearby contango.

In New York raw sugar futures staged a feeble attempt to recover but trade buying was countered by fund selling. Even though many regard the market as oversold the unbalanced world supply-demand picture continues to weigh heavily on prices.

ROMANIA - Sugar production in October 1996 amounted 91,529 tonnes, raw value, down from last year's 95,405 tonnes. This brought cumulative production in the first two months of the 1996/97 campaign (September/October) up to 94,444 tonnes, down from 101,689 tonnes produced in the like period the previous year. Total production in 1995/96 was 217,653 tonnes against 206,614 tonnes in 1994/95.

Sugar imports in October 1996 reached 53,670 tonnes, sharply up on last year's 5,045 tonnes. This brought cumulative imports in September/October 1996 up to 63,489 tonnes against 18,717 tonnes in 1995/96. Total imports in 1995/96 amounted to 327,159 tonnes compared to 275,178 tonnes in 1994/95. Major countries of origin in September/October 1996 were Brazil with 33,152 tonnes whites against nil, Cuba with 12,809 tonnes compared to nil and Austria with 5,561 tonnes against 4,175 tonnes.

FRANCE - Sugar consumption in July 1996 amounted to 223,149 tonnes, raw value, up from 182,287 tonnes in July 1995. This brought cumulative consumption in the first ten months of 1995/96 (October/July) up to 1.808 million tonnes against 1.777 million tonnes in the like period the previous year. Total consumption in 1994/95 reached 2.184 million tonnes compared to 2.208 million tonnes in 1993/94.

Sugar imports in September 1996 amounted to 40,173 tonnes, up from last year's 25,240 tonnes. This brought total imports in 1995/96 up to 476,602 tonnes against 364,140 tonnes in 1994/95 and 389,982 tonnes in 1993/94.

Major countries of origin in 1995/96 were Reunion with 171,651 tonnes raws against 154,938 tonnes, Swaziland with 66,047 tonnes, up from 50,142 tonnes and Belgium-Luxembourg with 36,972 tonnes whites compared to 13,607 tonnes.

Sugar exports in September 1996 amounted to 184,604 tonnes, up from 126,234 tonnes in September 1995. This brought total exports in 1995/96 up to 2.893 million tonnes, down from 3.067 million tonnes in 1994/95 and 2.819 million tonnes in 1993/94. Major countries of destination in 1995/96 were Belgium-Luxembourg with 469,620 tonnes whites, down from 943,719 tonnes, Spain with 247,171 tonnes against 223,140 tonnes, Turkey with 229,907 tonnes compared to 107,402 tonnes and Iran 225,701 tonnes compared to 196,012 tonnes.

RUSSIA - Ukraine has exported 1.2 million tonnes of white sugar to Russia in the first eleven months of 1996, compared to just over 1 million tonnes in the like period the previous year, a Russian official said.

Viktor Odoyevtsev, deputy head of the Foreign Economic Relations Ministry's domestic market protection department, said that this happened despite the fact that total Ukrainian sugar production in January/October 1996 fell by 421,000 tonnes from its 1995 level to 1.9 million tonnes.

He ascribed the higher exports to Russia to the fact that Ukraine had imported large amounts of raw sugar from Cuba for tolling which had found its way to Russia duty-free. Total Cuban raw sugar exports to the Ukraine in the first seven months of 1996 (January/July) amounted to 175,214 tonnes against nil in the like period the previous year.

The European Union awarded 31,000 tonnes of white sugar at a maximum refund of ECU 46.690 per 100 kg at its weekly tender on Wednesday. Cumulative awards so far made under the 1996/97 series of tenders for the period up to December 4 reached 1,183,750 tonnes, which compares to 1,332,725 tonnes last year.
